findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher never verifies the grant type (wrong indexes and inverted condition)
findings.body: The new matcher is meant to assert that an encoded access token ID (format `<2-char session><2-char token-type><2-char grant>:<uuid>`, e.g. `onrtac:1f65761e-...`) contains the expected grant shortcut. However the check reads `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Two defects: (1) the grant shortcut occupies character indexes 4-5, so it should be `substring(4, 6)`, not `substring(3, 5)`; (2) the condition is inverted — it returns `false` (no match) when the substring EQUALS the expected shortcut, instead of when it does NOT equal it. Because token-type shortcuts are `rt`/`lt`, `substring(3,5)` is always `t` + first char of the grant shortcut, which never equals the currently used expectations (`ac`, `dg`, `rt`, `ci`), so the matcher silently reduces to just the UUID check: all the updated event assertions (`expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectAuthReqIdToToken`) pass regardless of the encoded grant type, giving false confidence that the encoding works. Worse, if a grant shortcut starting with 't' were asserted (e.g. token-exchange `te`), the matcher would falsely reject valid tokens. The line should be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() method breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations at runtime
findings.body: Adding `String getShortcut();` as an abstract method to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface is a hard breaking change for any custom OAuth2 grant type provider compiled against the previous version. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` calls `gtf.getShortcut()` on every registered `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` during server startup, so an existing third-party grant provider that does not implement the new method will throw `AbstractMethodError` during `postInit`, failing server startup. Providing a default implementation (e.g. returning a derived or null shortcut handled gracefully) would avoid breaking deployed custom providers.

findings.title: Duplicated null check on grantType leaves rawTokenId unchecked
findings.body: The constructor contains `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` immediately after the identical check for grantType with the correct message. As a result `rawTokenId` is never null-checked (a null rawTokenId would later produce encoded IDs like `onrtac:null`), and if grantType were null the first check fires anyway, making the second statement dead code with a misleading message. The second statement should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`.

findings.title: Public copy constructor Context(Context) removed from grant SPI class
findings.body: The diff removes the public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor from `OAuth2GrantType.Context`, a public static class in the server-spi-private module. Nothing in the main codebase references it anymore, but any external/custom grant type implementation that clones a context (a reasonable pattern when wrapping or delegating grants) will no longer compile. If removal is intentional it should be called out in upgrade notes; otherwise the copy constructor should be kept and extended to copy the new `grantType` field.

findings.title: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException on malformed IDs instead of returning UNKNOWN context
findings.body: Decoding is asymmetric: a token ID without a colon (all pre-change tokens) is handled gracefully by returning an UNKNOWN `AccessTokenContext`, but any ID containing a colon that does not match the exact 6-character context format, or that contains unknown shortcuts, throws `IllegalArgumentException`. This method is intended to be used by endpoints (introspection, userinfo, account REST — per the follow-up issues #37662/#37117) that parse arbitrary, potentially attacker-supplied or older/foreign token IDs; an unhandled `IllegalArgumentException` there will surface as a 500 error. Consider returning an UNKNOWN context for undecodable IDs (or at least documenting the throws contract on `TokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId`).

findings.title: getShortcut() javadoc says '3-letters shortcut' but the format requires exactly 2 characters
findings.body: The javadoc states the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants", but the actual encoding format implemented in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` requires every shortcut to be exactly 2 characters long (`encodedContext.length() != 6` is enforced when decoding, 2 chars per type), and all built-in implementations return 2-character shortcuts (`ac`, `cc`, `rt`, `te`, ...). A provider author following the javadoc and returning a 3-character shortcut would produce token IDs that fail to decode. The javadoc should state that the shortcut must be exactly 2 characters and unique across grants.
